name: W3C
body: Preloaded HSTS, a lang on every page, and fast pages for real visitors. But the English, Japanese, and Chinese home pages are all titled just "W3C", and the Japanese description reads "Homepage".
lesson: Translate the title and description with the page. Each language version should say what it is, in its language.
summary: www.w3.org scores 86 out of 100 (B). 0 checks fail now, 20 are at risk, and 21 pass. Fix first: 20 pages have no canonical link.

fix.title: 20 pages have no canonical link
fix.evidence: /, /ja/, /zh-hans/, /standards/ and 16 more. Without it, tracking parameters and trailing slashes can split ranking signals.
fix.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="…"> with the page's own https URL.

fix.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

fix.title: No Organization or Person entity describes who is behind the site
fix.evidence: AI answers lean on this to name the brand, its logo, and its profiles. The page links 1 profile that could go in sameAs.
fix.fix: Add Organization (or Person) JSON-LD with name, url, logo, and sameAs. The fix kit has a draft.

fix.title: 1 title is shared by more than one page
fix.fix: Write a title that names what is different about each page.

fix.title: 3 images have no alt attribute
fix.fix: Describe informative images. Give decorative ones alt="".

works.title: Every internal link that was opened answered
AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http redirects permanently to https
The start page declares its language
The start page arrived in 151 ms
Share cards have a title, description, image, and URL
